_doc: HMTc Category 9 (Infant and Child Contact Products, Ages 0-5) compiler config. Method v2.0, contact-product form. Every cell names EXPLICIT register ids (a lookup, not a computation); the compiler takes the strictest (min) over ids that SHARE A BASIS. Basis is never conflated across the min: a migration limit and a total-content limit are different measured quantities, so total-content limits are carried as `companion` ceilings, published separately (like tHg/MeHg in seafood). iAs and MeHg are not-material for contact products (no inorganic-arsenic or methylmercury pathway); the arsenic/mercury cells are total element (tAs/tHg). APPLICABILITY (adversarial-audit 2026-08-10): pacifiers are EXCLUDED from the Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC (Annex I item 16, babies' soothers), so the pacifier row reads the EN 71-3 / 2009/48 Cat III migration values ACROSS via the EN 1400 soother standard, which requires them. Disposable diapers are EXCLUDED from REACH Annex XVII entry 72 (para 1(b), disposable textiles), so the diaper row reads the entry-72 values ACROSS (they bind reusable-cloth components directly). tAs/tHg on the toy rows bind the EU 2009/48 Cat III RAW limits (47/94), not the lower ASTM F963 nominal 25/60: ASTM incorporates an analytical-correction convention that EN 71-3:2013+ abolished, so the EU raw limit is the stricter ceiling as enforced. Antimony (Sb) is regulated in the toy-migration instruments but is not an HMTc panel analyte; it is screened, not published. See docs/governance/category-9-step0-lock.md.

pacifiers-and-sucking-teething-aids.name: Pacifiers and sucking/teething aids
pacifiers-and-sucking-teething-aids.governing_basis: EN 1400 soother standard, which requires the EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III Category III element-migration limits. Pacifiers are excluded from the Toy Safety Directive itself (Annex I item 16), so the migration limits are read across from the toy-migration regime via the EN 1400 route; the limit values are identical
pacifiers-and-sucking-teething-aids.native_basis_label: element migration from soother material (EN 1400 / EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg)

read_across.label: EN 1400 soother standard requires the EN 71-3 / 2009/48 Cat III lead migration limit (23 mg/kg); pacifiers are excluded from the Toy Safety Directive itself (Annex I item 16) but the soother standard requires this limit

EN 71-3 / 2009/48 Cat III total-arsenic migration limit (47 mg/kg), applied via EN 1400. ASTM F963's nominal 25 mg/kg is lower on paper but incorporates an analytical-correction convention EN 71-3 abolished, so the EU raw limit is the stricter ceiling as enforced

not_material.rationale: Contact-product arsenic limits regulate the total arsenic element; no toy-safety or soother instrument sets an inorganic-arsenic limit. Inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation with no migration counterpart. The tAs migration ceiling bounds the inorganic fraction.
not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration screen (EN 71-3 / ICP-MS); no reflex iAs speciation defined for mouthable articles.

read_across.label: EN 71-3 / 2009/48 Cat III cadmium migration limit (17 mg/kg), applied via EN 1400

EN 71-3 / 2009/48 Cat III total-mercury migration limit (94 mg/kg), applied via EN 1400. ASTM F963's nominal 60 mg/kg incorporates an analytical-correction convention EN 71-3 abolished, so the EU raw limit is the stricter ceiling as enforced

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is a marine-bioaccumulation speciation with no formation or migration pathway in a pacifier or teether. Every contact-product mercury limit is on total mercury. The tHg migration ceiling bounds any organomercury fraction.
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury migration screen (EN 71-3 / CV-AAS or ICP-MS).

read_across.label: EN 71-3 / 2009/48 Cat III nickel migration limit (930 mg/kg), applied via EN 1400
EN 71-3 / 2009/48 Cat III aluminium migration limit (28130 mg/kg), applied via EN 1400
EN 71-3 / 2009/48 Cat III hexavalent-chromium migration limit (0.053 mg/kg), applied via EN 1400
EN 71-3 / 2009/48 Cat III tin migration limit (180000 mg/kg — very permissive; Tier-2 screen), applied via EN 1400

teething-toys-teethers.name: Teething toys/teethers
teething-toys-teethers.governing_basis: toy migration (element migration from scraped-off toy material, EU 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III Category III; teething toys are toys and are directly governed by the Toy Safety Directive)
teething-toys-teethers.native_basis_label: element migration from scraped-off toy material (mg/kg material)
teething-toys-teethers.audit_exclude_basis: Category I|Category II|dry, brittle|liquid or sticky|coating|removable material|sticker|film

not_material.rationale: Contact-product arsenic limits regulate total arsenic; no toy-safety instrument sets an inorganic-arsenic limit. Bounded by the tAs migration ceiling.
Methylmercury has no formation or migration pathway in a teether. Bounded by the tHg migration ceiling.

teething-toys-teethers._note: tAs and tHg bind the EU 2009/48 Cat III raw limits (47/94), not ASTM F963 nominal (25/60): ASTM applies an analytical correction EN 71-3:2013+ abolished, so EU raw is stricter as enforced.

infant-bottles.name: Bottles (plastic, glass, stainless steel)
infant-bottles.governing_basis: food-contact specific migration into food (EU Regulation 10/2011 Annex II; 10/2011 is plastics-scope, applied to glass and stainless components as a conservative read-across since no stricter metal-FCM sovereign limit exists)

not_material.rationale: Food-contact migration limits regulate total arsenic; no inorganic-arsenic migration limit exists. Bounded by the tAs specific-migration ceiling.
No methylmercury pathway in a food-contact article. Bounded by the tHg specific-migration ceiling.

Ni.basis_label: specific migration into food (mg/kg food); stainless-steel drinkware additionally controlled by nickel release <=0.5 ug/cm2/week (former EU Directive 94/27/EC)

read_across.label: bounded by the total-chromium specific-migration limit (not detectable); hexavalent chromium is a fraction of total chromium, so the total-Cr ceiling bounds it

not_material.rationale: Tin migration is a tinplate/canned-food pathway; there is no tin source in a plastic, glass, or stainless food-contact bottle. Material only for tin-plated cans (Category 6/7).
not_material.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); periodic ICP-MS tin verification.

infant-bottle-nipples.name: Bottle nipples and spouts
infant-bottle-nipples.governing_basis: food-contact specific migration into food (EU Regulation 10/2011 Annex II; silicone/elastomer via the framework regulation)

not_material.rationale: No inorganic-arsenic migration limit; bounded by the tAs specific-migration ceiling.
No methylmercury pathway in a nipple/teat. Bounded by the tHg ceiling.

read_across.label: bounded by the total-chromium specific-migration limit (not detectable)

not_material.rationale: Inorganic tin has no migration pathway from a platinum-cured silicone or latex nipple; food-grade nipples are platinum-cured, not condensation-cured (which would use organotin catalysts). Certification requires platinum-cure documentation or an organotin screen; the separate EU toy organic-tin migration limit (Cat III 12 mg/kg) covers organotin, which the inorganic-Sn cell does not bound.
not_material.reference_method: Platinum-cure documentation; organotin (DBT/DOT) screen on condensation-cured elastomers; periodic ICP-MS inorganic tin verification.

sippy-cups-toddler-drinkware.name: Sippy cups and toddler drinkware components
sippy-cups-toddler-drinkware.governing_basis: food-contact specific migration into food (EU Regulation 10/2011 Annex II); stainless components additionally under nickel release

not_material.rationale: No inorganic-arsenic migration limit; bounded by tAs.
No methylmercury pathway. Bounded by tHg.

Ni.basis_label: specific migration into food (mg/kg food); stainless components additionally under nickel release <=0.5 ug/cm2/week (former EU Directive 94/27/EC)

read_across.label: bounded by the total-chromium specific-migration limit (not detectable)

not_material.rationale: No tin source in plastic or stainless drinkware; tinplate/canned-food pathway only.

infant-food-storage-items.name: Infant food-storage items (milk storage bags/containers)
infant-food-storage-items.governing_basis: food-contact specific migration into food (EU Regulation 10/2011 Annex II)

not_material.rationale: No inorganic-arsenic migration limit; bounded by tAs.
No methylmercury pathway. Bounded by tHg.

read_across.label: bounded by the total-chromium specific-migration limit (not detectable)

not_material.rationale: No tin source in a plastic milk-storage bag or container; tinplate/canned-food pathway only.

feeding-accessories-child-sized.name: Feeding accessories (spoons, plates, bowls — child-sized)
feeding-accessories-child-sized.governing_basis: food-contact specific migration into food (EU Regulation 10/2011 Annex II); painted/printed surfaces additionally under surface-coating content limits

not_material.rationale: No inorganic-arsenic migration limit; bounded by tAs.

companion.basis_label: surface-coating content (mg/kg of coating; cross-scope from Canada Toys Regulations SOR/2011-17)
companion.label: Surface-coating mercury ceiling (painted/printed tableware; read across from the toy surface-coating limit)

not_material.rationale: No methylmercury pathway. Bounded by tHg.

Ni.basis_label: specific migration into food (mg/kg food); stainless cutlery additionally under nickel release <=0.5 ug/cm2/week (former EU Directive 94/27/EC)

read_across.label: bounded by the total-chromium specific-migration limit (not detectable)

not_material.rationale: No tin source in plastic, stainless, or ceramic tableware; tinplate/canned-food pathway only.

diapers-and-components.name: Diapers and diaper components
diapers-and-components.governing_basis: skin-contact extractable metals (EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72). Entry 72 excludes disposable textiles (paragraph 1(b)), so its 1 mg/kg limits bind reusable-cloth diaper components directly and are read across as the benchmark for disposable-diaper skin-contact components; the absorbent core has no metal-migration pathway
diapers-and-components.native_basis_label: extractable metal after extraction (mg/kg homogeneous material)

read_across.label: EU REACH entry 72 extractable-lead limit (1 mg/kg after extraction). Entry 72 excludes disposable textiles (para 1(b)); the value binds reusable-cloth components directly and is read across as the benchmark for disposable skin-contact components
EU REACH entry 72 extractable-arsenic limit (1 mg/kg); read across per the disposable-textile exclusion

not_material.rationale: REACH textile limits regulate total arsenic; no inorganic-arsenic limit. Bounded by the tAs extraction ceiling.

read_across.label: EU REACH entry 72 extractable-cadmium limit (1 mg/kg); read across per the disposable-textile exclusion

not_material.rationale: No mercury source or migration pathway in absorbent-hygiene materials (cellulose fluff, super-absorbent polymer, PE/PP nonwoven). No jurisdiction sets a diaper mercury limit.
not_material.reference_method: Screen on incoming pulp/polymer certificates of analysis.

not_material.rationale: No methylmercury pathway in a diaper.

Standard diaper construction has no metallic skin-contact component. Where a product incorporates metallic snap fasteners (some training pants), those fasteners are screened under nickel release; the nonwoven and elastic materials have no nickel-release pathway.
not_material.reference_method: Component review; nickel-release screen (EN 1811) on any metallic fastener.

not_material.rationale: No aluminium source or migration pathway in absorbent-hygiene materials.

read_across.label: EU REACH entry 72 extractable-Cr(VI) limit (1 mg/kg); read across per the disposable-textile exclusion

not_material.rationale: No tin source in a diaper; tinplate/canned-food pathway only.
